answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using flow-based trust graphs. Each participant represents a vertex whose transaction quota scales with random-walk centrality seeded by verified peers. Adversaries incur the verifiable social cost of securing authentic inbound endorsements, as isolated Sybil subgraphs cannot amplify a valid trust signal. However, compromised seed agents can cause false reputation to spiral across clusters, and computing distributed graph walks adds routing latency.
